title: The violated line can be pinned
claim: The violated line can be pinned. For the octahedral knot spaces, an assignment violating one line is, in the bulk, a ground state of the triangular antiferromagnet with one defect triangle, and the violated line cannot always be moved locally: for both classes of adjacent line and every radius r <= 3 there are locally valid states (frozen cones of concentric alternating rings) from which no recolouring within radius r moves it there, and on K_8 every adjacent line of the central line has a whole-sphere state blocking the move at radius 2 and 3; random states always move (149 of 149 within radius 2). In label states (colourings by a 1-Lipschitz Z6 height through six sublattice patterns) every triangle is not-all-equal except at vortices, and a vortex's single monochromatic triangle is a line when its labels increase counterclockwise and a face when they decrease. So the Tseitin template for resolution width cannot be applied state by state; width Omega(sqrt n) reduces to a flat-state pursuit lemma for label states, which is open.
failure_conditions: A radius r <= 3 and adjacent line for which every locally valid single-defect configuration lets the violated line move within radius r.
An adjacent line of the central line of K_8 with no blocking whole-sphere state at r = 2 or 3.
A labelling within two consecutive values that colours a triangle monochromatically, or a vortex with other than one monochromatic triangle.
foundation_claim_scope: The bulk triangular lattice (balls of radius at most 4) and the octahedral knot space K_8; label states on the triangular lattice.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-06.
validation.status: statements 1-2 by exhibited configurations with exhaustive solver checks; statement 3 by hand and exhaustive check; no human or external review
validation.novelty: known-with-delta: frozen regions of dimer and antiferromagnet ground states are classical; the delta is that they obstruct the pebble-game width proof for these formulas, and the vortex reading of violated lines and full faces.
